sources.title: Guidelines for drinking-water quality: fourth edition incorporating the first, second and third addenda — chemical fact sheets
supports: WHO nitrate guideline value is 50 mg/L as nitrate ion (NO3-).
WHO nitrite guideline value is 3 mg/L as nitrite ion (NO2-).
WHO says the sum of nitrate concentration divided by 50 and nitrite concentration divided by 3 should not exceed 1 when both occur in drinking-water.
WHO publishes rounded conversions of 0.226 for nitrate ion to nitrate-nitrogen and 0.304 for nitrite ion to nitrite-nitrogen.
The 2026 consolidated edition's nitrate/nitrite fact sheet states an assessment date of 2016.

sources.title: Government Decree №58/2014 — Drinking Water Technical Regulation
sources.locator: Article 1(2)–(3); Article 2, Table 4, nitrate/nitrite rows; Article 2(21)
supports: For water within its scope, Table 4 lists nitrate at 50 mg/L as NO3- with a short-term exposure limiting sign.
For water within its scope, Table 4 lists nitrite at 0.2 mg/L as NO2- with a long-term exposure limiting sign.
Article 2(21) states a sum-of-ratios rule for multiple chemicals normalized under the same limiting sign, excluding radiological components.
Article 1(3) contains scope exclusions, including specified small individual-source supplies and certain mineral waters.

conversion_factors.precision_note: Both factors are published rounded conversions. Preserve original values and reporting basis; do not use converted rounded values alone for a near-threshold legal decision.

who_guidance.applies_to: WHO drinking-water guidance when both analytes occur in the same drinking-water sample

georgia_decree_58_2014.scope_note: Apply only after confirming Article 1 scope and exclusions for the particular supply.

multiple_chemicals_rule.condition: sum concentration/limit ratios only for multiple chemicals normalized under the same limiting sign; radiological components are excluded
multiple_chemicals_rule.interpretation: The table assigns nitrate and nitrite different limiting signs. The text therefore does not support automatically importing the WHO nitrate-plus-nitrite combined ratio as a Georgian legal pass/fail rule. Obtain independent Georgian legal review before implementing a local combined compliance calculation.

comparability_guards: Do not apply the WHO combined ratio to raw groundwater or another matrix without confirming that the sample is drinking-water within the guidance scope.
Do not combine nitrate and nitrite values from different sample identifiers or collection times.
The executable WHO ratio helper requires both analytes on their native ion basis in mg/L and one pseudonymous sample identifier, timezone-aware collection timestamp and drinking-water matrix.
Do not treat the WHO combined ratio as a Georgian legal compliance decision; Decree 58/2014 lists different limiting signs for nitrate and nitrite.
Do not use rounded nitrogen-basis conversion factors as the sole basis for near-threshold legal decisions.
No sample-level Georgian nitrate/nitrite data were available; no local ratio, exposure estimate or compliance result is calculated.
